greek: Καὶ ἐξάρας Ιακωβ τοὺς πόδας ἐπορεύθη εἰς γῆν ἀνατολῶν πρὸς Λαβαν τὸν υἱὸν Βαθουηλ τοῦ Σύρου ἀδελφὸν δὲ Ρεβεκκας μητρὸς Ιακωβ καὶ Ησαυ.
hint: Jacob sets out for the land of the east, to Laban son of Bethuel the Syrian, Rebekah's brother.

notes.text: The Hebrew idiom *wayyiśśāʾ raglāyw*, *he lifted his feet*, carried over word for word.
Middle Liddell heads the entry with the Epic ἐξαείρω.

reading: And [[having lifted up|having lifted up, having lifted off the earth, having raised in dignity and exalted, having raised and aroused and stirred up|ἐξαίρω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[the feet|the feet, the talons, the feet of a hill|πούς]] [[was driven|was driven, was carried, went, walked, marched, went across and passed|πορεύομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[earth|earth, land, ground|γῆ]] [[of risings|of risings, of rises, of the quarter of sunrise, of the east|ἀνατολή]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[name:Λαβαν]] the son of [[name:Βαθουηλ]] of the [[name:Σύρου]] [[son of the same mother|a son of the same mother, a brother, a near kinsman|ἀδελφός]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], of [[name:Ρεβεκκας]] [[of mother|of mother, of dam, of source|μήτηρ]] of [[name:Ιακωβ]] and of [[name:Ησαυ]].

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")
(Βαθουηλ, from Hebrew Bĕtûʾēl, of uncertain meaning)
(Σύρος, the man of Συρία, Syria; the Hebrew has ʾărammî, the Aramean)
(Ρεβεκκα, from Hebrew Ribqâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Ησαυ, from Hebrew ʿĒśāw, usually connected with śēʿār, "hair")

greek: καὶ ὁρᾷ καὶ ἰδοὺ φρέαρ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ, ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ τρία ποίμνια προβάτων ἀναπαυόμενα ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ φρέατος ἐκείνου ἐπότιζον τὰ ποίμνια, λίθος δὲ ἦν μέγας ἐπὶ τῷ στόματι τοῦ φρέατος,
hint: Jacob sees a well in the plain, three flocks of sheep resting by it, and a great stone over its mouth.

notes.text: The present, in a past narrative: the historic present.
One sense, *a flock*; Middle Liddell's second, of disciples, glosses nothing.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, *at the same place*.

hint: The custom at the well: once all the flocks are gathered, the stone is rolled off, the sheep watered, the stone put back.

notes.text: Four imperfects of custom: what was done again and again.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ιακωβ Ἀδελφοί, πόθεν ἐστὲ ὑμεῖς; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἐκ Χαρραν ἐσμέν.
hint: Jacob hails the shepherds as brothers and asks where they are from; they are from Haran.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to them [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[sons of the same mother|sons of the same mother, brothers, near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]], [[whence|whence, from what source, whence and wherefore|πόθεν]] are you; the ones [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of [[name:Χαρραν]] we are.

names.gloss: (Χαρραν, from Hebrew Ḥārān, of uncertain meaning)

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Γινώσκετε Λαβαν τὸν υἱὸν Ναχωρ; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Γινώσκομεν.
hint: Jacob asks whether they know Laban son of Nahor, and they do.

notes.text: Laban is Nahor's grandson; the Greek says *son*, as the Hebrew does.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to them [[you learn to know|you learn to know, you perceive, you mark, you learn, you discern and distinguish|γινώσκω]] [[name:Λαβαν]] the son of [[name:Ναχωρ]]; the ones [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[we learn to know|we learn to know, we perceive, we mark, we learn, we discern and distinguish|γινώσκω]].

names.gloss: (Ναχωρ, from Hebrew Nāḥôr, of uncertain meaning)

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ὑγιαίνει; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ὑγιαίνει. καὶ ἰδοὺ Ραχηλ ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτοῦ ἤρχετο μετὰ τῶν προβάτων.
hint: Laban is well, they tell him, and his daughter Rachel is coming with the sheep.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *hăšālôm lô*, *is there peace to him*; the Greek asks after his health.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος before it, and adds the end of verse 9 here.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ιακωβ Ἔτι ἐστὶν ἡμέρα πολλή, οὔπω ὥρα συναχθῆναι τὰ κτήνη· ποτίσαντες τὰ πρόβατα ἀπελθόντες βόσκετε.
hint: Jacob points out that it is still broad day, too early to gather the herds, and tells them to water the sheep and graze them.

notes.text: The entry opens with *period*, whether of the year, month, or day; *a part of the year, a season* is its first numbered sense.
The accusative subject of the passive infinitive συναχθῆναι.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

hint: The shepherds cannot water the sheep until all of them have gathered and the stone is rolled off the well.

hint: Rachel comes up with her father's sheep, which she herds, while Jacob is still speaking.

greek: ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς εἶδεν Ιακωβ τὴν Ραχηλ θυγατέρα Λαβαν ἀδελφοῦ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ πρόβατα Λαβαν ἀδελφοῦ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσελθὼν Ιακωβ ἀπεκύλισεν τὸν λίθον ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ φρέατος καὶ ἐπότισεν τὰ πρόβατα Λαβαν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ.
hint: Seeing Rachel, Jacob rolls the stone from the well and waters the sheep of Laban, three times named his mother's brother.

greek: καὶ ἐφίλησεν Ιακωβ τὴν Ραχηλ καὶ βοήσας τῇ φωνῇ αὐτοῦ ἔκλαυσεν.
hint: Jacob kisses Rachel, cries aloud, and weeps.

notes.text: φιλέω, *to love, regard with affection*, where the Hebrew has *kiss*, as through GEN 27.

hint: Jacob tells Rachel he is her father's brother and Rebekah's son, and she runs to tell her father.

notes.text: Jacob is Laban's nephew; the Greek, with the Hebrew, says *brother*, of kinship at large.

hint: Laban will not have a brother serve for nothing, and asks Jacob to name his wage.

greek: καὶ συνέλαβεν ἔτι καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ εἶπεν Ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ πρὸς ἐμοῦ ἔσται ὁ ἀνήρ μου, ἔτεκον γὰρ αὐτῷ τρεῖς υἱούς· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Λευι.
hint: Leah bears Levi, expecting her husband to be hers now that she has borne him three sons.

notes.text: πρός with the genitive, *on my side*, of what belongs to one.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τέτοκα, the perfect, and ἐκλήθη, *was called*, for ἐκάλεσεν.

greek: καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτι ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ εἶπεν Νῦν ἔτι τοῦτο ἐξομολογήσομαι κυρίῳ· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ιουδα. καὶ ἔστη τοῦ τίκτειν.
hint: Leah bears a fourth son, Judah, acknowledging the Lord, and then stops bearing.

notes.text: The Hebrew hears the name in *yādâ*, *praise, give thanks*, which the Greek keeps in ἐξομολογήσομαι.
ἵστημι in the intransitive aorist, with the articular infinitive: she stood off from bearing.
